result.title: Nowcasting of Tropical Cyclone Wind Fields and Intensity from Geostationary Imagery
result.comment: Accepted as a workshop paper at Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning, NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: High-resolution tropical cyclone surface wind speeds derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations can support storm structure and intensity modelling, but remain spatially and temporally sparse and unavailable near-real-time. Geostationary satellites capture cloud tops continuously in space and time, but do not directly resolve surface winds. Here, we present simple neural networks to predict 2D wind fields and storm-scale intensity metrics from geostationary imagery. Through a series of ablation studies, we find that joint prediction of 2D fields and scalar metrics from the model latent space improves the retrieval of the (radius of) maximum wind, especially for rapid intensification events.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作用简单神经网络从静止卫星云图同时预测热带气旋二维风场与风暴尺度强度指标，并通过消融实验考察共享 latent 空间联合预测的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 原文从同一 latent 空间联合预测稠密场与标量指标、并以消融检验哪类预测改善标量检索，可供核查多任务监督如何影响 latent 状态中的信息保留与贡献分配，但领域相距较远，需人工判断可迁移性。
